newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO-Russia meeting goes ahead after hitches.
newsitem.headline: NATO-Russia meeting goes ahead after hitches.

text.p: The inaugural meeting of the NATO-Russia partnership council took place on Friday after last-gasp efforts by diplomats ironed out protocol wrangles to do with who chaired the event.
The meeting of alliance ambassadors with their Russian counterpart had looked in jeopardy until late on Thursday with both sides unhappy with chairing arrangements, alliance sources said.

A joint NATO-Russia statement said ambassadors adopted rules of procedure for their new council, created as a salve to Moscow's anxieties over the Western alliance's eastwards enlargement, and agreed work plans ahead of its first ministerial-level meeting slated for late September in New York.
Friday's meeting was the first since the two sides signed a Founding Act establishing a new post-Cold War relationship in May. The next is scheduled for September 11, the statement said.

The council was to have met in Brussels on Thursday at ambassadorial level, but NATO and the Russians were unable to agree the mechanics of how a rotating presidency involving both sides and the alliance secretary general would work in practice.
The deal conjured up by diplomats has the secretary general opening and closing the meeting with a three-way rotation of the presidency for all agenda items in between, sources said.
